subproblem.title: Derivative at 0 of the Gram-formula projection
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, iota : R^n -> R^(n+l) and kappa : R^l -> R^(n+l) continuous linear maps, and tau : L(R^n, R^(n+l)) -> L(R^(n+l), R^n) a continuous linear map (spaces of continuous linear maps carry the operator norm; R^k = Rn k, R^(n+l) = Amb n l) such that (T) <tau(L) w, v> = <w, L v> for all L in L(R^n, R^(n+l)), w in R^(n+l), v in R^n; (I) <iota v, iota u> = <v, u> for all v, u in R^n; (O) <iota v, kappa z> = 0 for all v in R^n, z in R^l. For A in L(R^n, R^l) put J_A := iota + kappa o A and F(A) := J_A o (Ring.inverse(tau(J_A) o J_A) o tau(J_A)), where Ring.inverse is taken in the ring L(R^n, R^n) whose multiplication is composition (Ring.inverse x is the two-sided inverse of x when x is a unit and 0 otherwise). Then for every H in L(R^n, R^l): (fderiv R F 0) H = iota o tau(kappa o H) + kappa o H o tau(iota).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (ι : Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (κ : Rn ℓ →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (τ : (Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Amb n ℓ →L[ℝ] Rn n)), (∀ (L : Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (w : Amb n ℓ) (v : Rn n), inner ℝ (τ L w) v = inner ℝ w (L v)) → (∀ v u : Rn n, inner ℝ (ι v) (ι u) = inner ℝ v u) → (∀ (v : Rn n) (z : Rn ℓ), inner ℝ (ι v) (κ z) = 0) → ∀ H : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, fderiv ℝ (fun A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ => (ι + κ ∘L A) ∘L Ring.inverse (τ (ι + κ ∘L A) ∘L (ι + κ ∘L A)) ∘L τ (ι + κ ∘L A)) 0 H = ι ∘L τ (κ ∘L H) + κ ∘L H ∘L τ ι
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3 (the identities for pi := tau(iota)) and step 5 (derivatives at 0), carried out for an abstract triple (iota, kappa, tau) satisfying (T), (I), (O). Nondegeneracy below means ext_inner_right: if <a, u> = <b, u> for all u, then a = b.

1. Algebraic facts. Put pi := tau(iota).
 (a) pi o iota = 1 (the identity of R^n): for v, u in R^n, <pi(iota v), u> = <iota v, iota u> = <v, u> by (T) and (I); nondegeneracy gives pi(iota v) = v.
 (b) pi(kappa z) = 0 for every z in R^l: for all u, <pi(kappa z), u> = <kappa z, iota u> = <iota u, kappa z> = 0 = <0, u> by (T), symmetry of the real inner product (real_inner_comm) and (O).
 (c) tau(kappa o H')(iota v) = 0 for all H' in L(R^n, R^l) and v in R^n: for all u, <tau(kappa o H')(iota v), u> = <iota v, kappa(H' u)> = 0 = <0, u> by (T) and (O).

2. The map J. Let K := ContinuousLinearMap.compL R (Rn n) (Rn l) (Amb n l) kappa, the continuous linear map L(R^n, R^l) -> L(R^n, R^(n+l)) with K(A) = kappa o A (definitionally). J_A = iota + K(A) is a constant plus a continuous linear map, so A |-> J_A has derivative K at 0 (K.hasFDerivAt and HasFDerivAt.const_add). Also J_0 = iota + kappa o 0 = iota.

3. The map tau(J). Since tau is continuous linear, the chain rule (tau.hasFDerivAt.comp) shows that A |-> tau(J_A) has derivative tau o K at 0, i.e. H' |-> tau(kappa o H').

4. The Gram map G_A := tau(J_A) o J_A has derivative 0 at 0. By the product rule for compositions of operator-valued maps (HasFDerivAt.clm_comp: if c has derivative c' and d has derivative d' at 0, then A |-> c(A) o d(A) has derivative H' |-> c(0) o d'(H') + c'(H') o d(0) at 0), G has at 0 the derivative H' |-> tau(J_0) o (kappa o H') + tau(kappa o H') o J_0 = pi o kappa o H' + tau(kappa o H') o iota. Evaluated at any v in R^n this is pi(kappa(H' v)) + tau(kappa o H')(iota v) = 0 + 0 by 1(b) and 1(c). Hence this derivative is the zero map, and G has derivative 0 at 0. (In Lean: convert (hT.clm_comp hJ) using 1, then ext H' v and simp using 1(b), 1(c) and K(A) = kappa o A.)

5. G_0 = tau(J_0) o J_0 = pi o iota = 1 by step 2 and 1(a).

6. The inverse. L(R^n, R^n) is a complete normed ring, so the instance HasSummableGeomSeries holds and hasFDerivAt_ringInverse, applied to the unit 1, shows that Ring.inverse has a derivative D at 1 = G_0 (step 5). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp) the map A |-> R_A := Ring.inverse(G_A) has derivative D o 0 = 0 at 0 (ContinuousLinearMap.comp_zero). Moreover R_0 = Ring.inverse 1 = 1 (Ring.inverse_one).

7. The map F. F(A) = J_A o (R_A o tau(J_A)). Applying HasFDerivAt.clm_comp first to R and tau(J) (steps 6 and 3) and then to J (step 2) and that product, F has at 0 the derivative
 H |-> J_0 o (R_0 o tau(kappa o H) + 0 o tau(J_0)) + (kappa o H) o (R_0 o tau(J_0)),
 and HasFDerivAt.fderiv identifies it with fderiv R F 0. Substituting J_0 = iota (so tau(J_0) = tau(iota)) and R_0 = 1 (the identity map: ContinuousLinearMap.one_def, id_comp), dropping the zero term, and using K(H) = kappa o H and associativity of composition (comp_assoc), we get (fderiv R F 0) H = iota o tau(kappa o H) + kappa o H o tau(iota).
proof_key_steps: pi := tau(iota) satisfies pi o iota = 1, pi o kappa = 0 and tau(kappa o H') o iota = 0, by (T), (I), (O) and nondegeneracy
A |-> J_A = iota + kappa o A has derivative K = compL kappa at 0, and A |-> tau(J_A) has derivative tau o K
Product rule: G_A = tau(J_A) o J_A has derivative pi o kappa o H' + tau(kappa o H') o iota = 0 at 0, and G_0 = 1
hasFDerivAt_ringInverse at the unit 1 with the chain rule: R_A = Ring.inverse(G_A) has derivative 0 at 0, and R_0 = 1
Product rule twice on F(A) = J_A o (R_A o tau(J_A)), then simplify: fderiv F 0 H = iota o tau(kappa o H) + kappa o H o tau(iota)

subproblem.title: Inner product of graph points
subproblem.statement: For all natural numbers n, l, all x, x' in R^n and all y, y' in R^l: <graphPoint x y, graphPoint x' y'> = <x, x'> + <y, y'>, where < , > is the real inner product of the Euclidean spaces R^k = EuclideanSpace R (Fin k) and graphPoint x y in R^(n+l) = Amb n l has first n coordinates x and last l coordinates y.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (x x' : Rn n) (y y' : Rn ℓ), inner ℝ (graphPoint x y) (graphPoint x' y') = inner ℝ x x' + inner ℝ y y'
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2 (inner products of graph points).

1. The inner product of EuclideanSpace R (Fin m) is the coordinate sum <a, b> = sum_k <a_k, b_k> (PiLp.inner_apply), where <a_k, b_k> is the inner product of the real scalars a_k, b_k. Apply this to each of the three inner products in the claim.

2. Unfold graphPoint: graphPoint x y = toLp 2 (Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y)), so its k-th coordinate is Fin.append x y k, and likewise for graphPoint x' y'. Split the sum over Fin (n+l) into its castAdd and natAdd parts (Fin.sum_univ_add): sum_{k : Fin (n+l)} f k = sum_{i : Fin n} f (Fin.castAdd l i) + sum_{j : Fin l} f (Fin.natAdd n j).

3. At castAdd indices the coordinates of graphPoint x y and graphPoint x' y' are x_i and x'_i (Fin.append_left); at natAdd indices they are y_j and y'_j (Fin.append_right). Hence <graphPoint x y, graphPoint x' y'> = sum_i <x_i, x'_i> + sum_j <y_j, y'_j>, which equals <x, x'> + <y, y'> by step 1. (In Lean the single call simp only [graphPoint, PiLp.inner_apply, Fin.sum_univ_add, Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right] closes the goal.)
proof_key_steps: Inner product on EuclideanSpace is the coordinate sum (PiLp.inner_apply)
Split the sum over Fin (n+l) into castAdd and natAdd parts (Fin.sum_univ_add)
Coordinates there are x_i, x'_i resp. y_j, y'_j (Fin.append_left/right), giving <x, x'> + <y, y'>

audit.reason: The unconditional inner-product identity exactly matches its Lean proposition. Expanding PiLp inner products and splitting the finite coordinate sum proves it directly, including zero-dimensional cases, without circular dependencies.

subproblem.title: Graph points split as iota x + kappa y with continuous linear iota, kappa
subproblem.statement: For all natural numbers n, l there exist continuous linear maps iota : R^n -> R^(n+l) and kappa : R^l -> R^(n+l) such that graphPoint x y = iota x + kappa y for all x in R^n and y in R^l. Here R^k = EuclideanSpace R (Fin k) = Rn k, R^(n+l) = Amb n l, and graphPoint x y = toLp 2 (Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y)) is the point of R^(n+l) whose first n coordinates are those of x and whose last l coordinates are those of y.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), ∃ (ι : Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (κ : Rn ℓ →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ), ∀ (x : Rn n) (y : Rn ℓ), graphPoint x y = ι x + κ y
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1 (splitting graphPoint).

1. Let Phi : R^n x R^l -> R^(n+l) be the inverse of Mathlib's continuous linear equivalence EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd : R^(n+l) ≃L[R] R^n x R^l (with n + l coordinates split as n then l), viewed as a continuous linear map. Define iota := Phi ∘L ContinuousLinearMap.inl R (Rn n) (Rn l) and kappa := Phi ∘L ContinuousLinearMap.inr R (Rn n) (Rn l). They are continuous linear as compositions of continuous linear maps, and iota x = Phi (x, 0), kappa y = Phi (0, y) (ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, inl_apply, inr_apply).

2. Claim: graphPoint x y = Phi (x, y) for all x in R^n, y in R^l. Two vectors of R^(n+l) are equal when all their coordinates agree (ext). By Fin.addCases every index of Fin (n+l) is Fin.castAdd l j with j : Fin n, or Fin.natAdd n k with k : Fin l. At castAdd l j the coordinate of graphPoint x y is Fin.append x y (castAdd l j) = x j (Fin.append_left), and the coordinate of Phi (x, y) is also x j, because finAddEquivProd reindexes along finSumFinEquiv and then splits into the Sum.inl/Sum.inr parts (finSumFinEquiv_symm_apply_castAdd). At natAdd n k both coordinates equal y k (Fin.append_right; finSumFinEquiv_symm_apply_natAdd). In Lean each of the two cases closes by simp [graphPoint, Phi].

3. Therefore graphPoint x y = Phi (x, y) = Phi ((x, 0) + (0, y)) = Phi (x, 0) + Phi (0, y) = iota x + kappa y, using (x, 0) + (0, y) = (x + 0, 0 + y) = (x, y) (Prod.mk_add_mk, add_zero, zero_add) and additivity of Phi (map_add). So iota and kappa witness the existential.
proof_key_steps: Phi := (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd).symm as a continuous linear map; iota := Phi ∘L inl, kappa := Phi ∘L inr
graphPoint x y = Phi (x, y) by ext, Fin.addCases and Fin.append_left/right (simp [graphPoint])
Phi (x, y) = Phi (x, 0) + Phi (0, y) = iota x + kappa y by additivity of Phi

subproblem.title: Coordinate formula for a transpose
subproblem.statement: For natural numbers n, m and continuous linear maps L : R^n -> R^m and T : R^m -> R^n (R^k = EuclideanSpace R (Fin k) = Rn k) such that <T w, v> = <w, L v> for all w in R^m and v in R^n: T w = sum_{i<n} <L e_i, w> e_i for every w in R^m, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 is the i-th standard basis vector of R^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n m : ℕ) (L : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn m) (T : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn n), (∀ (w : Rn m) (v : Rn n), inner ℝ (T w) v = inner ℝ w (L v)) → ∀ w : Rn m, T w = ∑ i : Fin n, inner ℝ (L (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) w • EuclideanSpace.single i 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 6(b) (expansion u = sum_i u_i e_i and nondegeneracy), carried out for an arbitrary L in place of kappa o H.

1. By nondegeneracy of the inner product (ext_inner_right) it suffices to show <T w, u> = <sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i, u> for every u in R^n.

2. Fix u in R^n and expand u = sum_i u_i e_i in the standard orthonormal basis (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr for EuclideanSpace.basisFun, whose basis vectors are the e_i and whose coordinates are the u_i).

3. Left side: <T w, u> = <w, L u> by the hypothesis. Substituting u = sum_i u_i e_i and using linearity of L (map_sum, map_smul) and of the inner product in its second argument (inner_sum, real_inner_smul_right): <w, L u> = sum_i u_i <w, L e_i>.

4. Right side: by linearity in the first argument (sum_inner, real_inner_smul_left), <sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i, u> = sum_i <L e_i, w> <e_i, u>, and <e_i, u> = u_i (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left, since conj 1 = 1).

5. The two sums agree termwise, u_i <w, L e_i> = <L e_i, w> u_i, by symmetry of the real inner product (real_inner_comm) and commutativity of multiplication. By step 1, T w = sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i.
proof_key_steps: Reduce to <T w, u> = <sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i, u> for all u (ext_inner_right)
Expand u = sum_i u_i e_i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun, OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr)
<T w, u> = <w, L u> = sum_i u_i <w, L e_i>, and <sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i, u> = sum_i <L e_i, w> u_i
The sums agree termwise by symmetry of the real inner product
